elements.element: The licences extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The added language extends the licences to Corio's affiliates only upon written notice to Commerce One. This satisfies the notice-based fallback, not the preferred unconditional affiliate coverage.

elements.element: The licences extend to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No operative language extends any licence to contractors acting for Corio.
Section 2.2 expressly grants a “fully paid up, perpetual” licence.
Section 2.2's fully paid-up licence is perpetual but is not stated to be irrevocable. Section 2.1 is irrevocable but is described as fee-bearing rather than fully paid-up.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence appears in the supplied operative language: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 grant perpetual licences. The condition requiring a subscription-specific termination restriction is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: The grants remain nontransferable except under Section 14.1. That section permits only specified M&A-related assignments and still requires consent where the transaction involves the other party's direct competitor, so it does not provide general successor transferability.

elements.element: Affiliates are covered upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The added Affiliates provision expressly states that, upon written notice to Commerce One, the Section 2 licences extend to Corio's affiliates.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 generally permits assignment in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all relevant assets, but withdraws that no-consent right when the transaction involves the other party's direct competitor. The fallback is therefore not met for every M&A successor transaction.

result.reason: The redline adds the required notice-based affiliate extension but omits contractor coverage and irrevocability for the fully paid-up licence. The supplied grants are perpetual rather than subscription-based. Section 14.1 provides substantial M&A assignment rights, but its direct-competitor consent exception prevents complete satisfaction of the stated successor-transfer requirements. Because no complete preferred or fallback level is achieved, the redline is not minimal as defined, although the affiliate addition is otherwise clear and does not disrupt unrelated commercial terms.
